To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the proposed phantom can be utilized to evaluate the effects of PVEs on diffusion tensor parameters and (2) the diffusion tensor parameters of fornix and cingulum in healthy volunteers are affected by PVEs
the proposed DTI‐based approach for the analysis of fine brain anatomy is robust against PVEs.

(1) the use of the DTI‐based fiber tracking algorithm is a promising approach to investigate the fornix in vivo, (2) the use of a diffusion phantom with a resolution of 0.7 mm × 0.7mm × 3 mm can be recommended for the investigation of the resolution dependence of diffusion parameters, and (3) the use of this phantom is especially helpful to investigate the resolution dependence of the apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) in fine structures
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of methods to reduce PVEs in diffusion‐imaging‐based analysis of brain structures.
the investigation of the influence of PVEs on the diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) analysis of white matter fiber bundles and their quantification.

the development and validation of methods that allow the quantification of microstructures in the presence of partial volume effects and the investigation of the influence of PVEs and the spatial resolution on the diffusion imaging parameters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the diffusion imaging‐derived analysis of fine brain structure is feasible and that the PVEs are not a limiting factor for this analysis, but the PVEs need to be considered.
the diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) technique can be used in the analysis of fine structures, but the results must be interpreted with caution.
PVE is an important issue in the diffusion imaging of the brain and needs to be addressed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the diffusion imaging‐related resolution effects are not negligible and have to be considered in the interpretation of the diffusion parameters.
we have shown that the resolution of diffusion‐based imaging is limited by partial volume effects.
the diffusion parameters of the fornix and cingulum are affected by the partial volume effect.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a specialized diffusion tensor (DT) phantom with a high spatial resolution can be used to quantify PVEs in the DT‐based analysis of the fornix and cingulum.

diffusion parameters can be measured with high precision and reproducibility in a small structure like the fornix using the diffusion‐weighted imaging (DWI)‐based approach with the use of a specialized diffusion tensor (DT) phantom.
the PVEs can be significantly reduced with a specialized DT‐phantom, which is a major step towards the clinical application of diffusion‐based imaging biomarkers for fine brain structures.
